record.original_question: Which projective varieties M in projective space P^n have maximum likelihood degree 1, meaning that for generic data vector (u0, u1, ..., un) the restriction of the likelihood function L(p0, p1, ..., pn) = p0^u0 · p1^u1 · ... · pn^un / (p0 + p1 + ··· + pn)^(u0 + u1 + ··· + un) to M has exactly one complex critical point after excluding singular points of M and points where L has poles or zeros?

evidence.quote: Specific Problem: Find a geometric characterization of those projective varieties whose maximum likelihood degree (ML degree) is equal to one.

The ML degree of the variety M is the number of complex critical points of the restriction of the likelihood function L to M. Here we disregard singular points of M, we only count critical points that are not poles or zeros of L, and u0, u1, . . . , un are assumed to be generic.
The corresponding likelihood function is defined as L(p0, p1, . . . , pn) = p0^u0 · p1^u1 · p2^u2 · · · · · pn^un / (p0+p1+ · · · +pn)^(u0+u1+···+un).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in complex projective space $\mathbb{P}^n$ with homogeneous coordinates $(p_0:p_1:\cdots:p_n)$. For a generic data vector $(u_0,u_1,\ldots,u_n) \in \mathbb{Z}^{n+1}$, define the likelihood function
$$L(p_0,p_1,\ldots,p_n) \;=\; \frac{p_0^{u_0}\, p_1^{u_1}\cdots p_n^{u_n}}{(p_0+p_1+\cdots+p_n)^{u_0+u_1+\cdots+u_n}},$$
which is a rational function on $\mathbb{P}^n$. For an irreducible projective variety $M \subset \mathbb{P}^n$, the maximum likelihood degree (ML degree) of $M$ is defined to be the number of complex critical points of the restriction $L|_M$, where one excludes singular points of $M$ and points at which $L$ has a pole or a zero, and where $(u_0,\ldots,u_n)$ is generic.

Give a geometric characterization of all irreducible projective varieties $M \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ whose ML degree equals $1$.
artifact.status_search_result: June Huh (arXiv:1301.2732, "Varieties with maximum likelihood degree one") characterized varieties of ML degree one as exactly the images of reduced A-discriminantal varieties under monomial maps with finite fibers, with the corresponding maximum likelihood estimator given by Kapranov's Horn uniformization. This provides the geometric characterization sought.

status_evidence.title: Varieties with maximum likelihood degree one
status_evidence.snippet: Algebraic varieties with maximum likelihood degree one are exactly the images of reduced A-discriminantal varieties under monomial maps with finite fibers.
status_evidence.claim: Huh provides a geometric characterization of varieties with ML degree one via Horn uniformization.

status_evidence.title: Likelihood Geometry — Huh and Sturmfels
status_evidence.snippet: Varieties of ML degree one are characterized as images of A-discriminantal varieties under monomial maps with finite fibers.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization is established and surveyed in subsequent work.
